prompt: Implement number_to_words(n) in solution.py. n is an integer from 0 to 999999. Return the English words in lower case, words separated by single spaces. Do not use the word and. Numbers from 21 to 99 that are not round tens are hyphenated, for example twenty-one and seventy-three. Examples, 0 is zero, 100 is one hundred, 305 is three hundred five, 1234 is one thousand two hundred thirty-four. Run python -m pytest -q test_visible.py.
diff:
diff --git a/solution.py b/solution.py

--- a/solution.py
+++ b/solution.py
@@ -1,2 +1,25 @@
-def number_to_words(n):
-    raise NotImplementedError
+def number_to_words(n: int) -> str:
+    ones = ['zero','one','two','three','four','five','six','seven','eight','nine',
+            'ten','eleven','twelve','thirteen','fourteen','fifteen','sixteen',
+            'seventeen','eighteen','nineteen']
+    tens = ['','','twenty','thirty','forty','fifty','sixty','seventy','eighty','ninety']
+
+    def below_1000(num: int) -> str:
+        if num < 20:
+            return ones[num]
+        if num < 100:
+            t = tens[num // 10]
+            r = num % 10
+            return t if r == 0 else f'{t}-{ones[r]}'
+        h = ones[num // 100] + ' hundred'
+        r = num % 100
+        return h if r == 0 else f'{h} {below_1000(r)}'
+
+    if n < 1000:
+        return below_1000(n)
+    thousands = n // 1000
+    remainder = n % 1000
+    result = below_1000(thousands) + ' thousand'
+    if remainder:
+        result += ' ' + below_1000(remainder)
+    return result
